title: Epochal stream segmentation and SOMP (Structured Output Micro-Protocol) - PRD draft
content:
Overview:

This PRD describes a design sketch for a hybrid streaming surface that splits long-running model output into ordered "epochs" (epochal segmentation) and a lightweight Structured Output Micro-Protocol (SOMP) for deterministic tool-calling and compact structured frames. The goal is an ergonomic SDK surface that:
- supports low-latency incremental consumption for UIs and agents,
- enables safe, observable, and resumable tool calls without blocking the main stream,
- carries structured payloads that are small, parseable, and backward-compatible across client versions.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Many customer integrations need: progressive UI updates, deterministic tool call handshake, and the ability to resume interrupted sessions. Current partial-response approaches either send raw text fragments (prone to ambiguity) or heavy JSON blobs (too large, brittle).
- Tool-calling today is often blocking or tightly coupled to a single response frame; this leads to retries, duplicated tool-side effects, and poor developer ergonomics when network flakiness occurs.

Goals (what success looks like):
- SDK exposes a simple progressive iterator that yields epoch frames and a safe tool-call API that guarantees at-least-once visibility but offers idempotency tokens to tool adapters.
- End-to-end resume: after a network interruption the client can reconnect and request: a) the latest committed epoch id, b) an in-progress tool-call state, c) a small checkpoint of the KV-prefix needed for deterministic continuation.
- Structured frames are compact (under 512 bytes typical) using a minimal binary-friendly encoding (SOMP textual flavor) and include schema version, epoch id, sequence offset, and optional action descriptors.
- Telemetry: per-epoch latency, per-tool-call success/failure, and client-side rejoin metrics are visible in Console.

Non-goals:
- This draft does not attempt to design a full new schema language or strongly typed RPC layer. SOMP is intentionally small and versioned.
- Not addressing cross-model orchestration (that lives in routing layer).

Assumptions:
- Most host responses are still text-first; SOMP will be used to annotate chunks and machine-parsable actions, not replace free-text channels.
- Customers will want both server-stream (SSE/websocket) and client-poll fallback.

User stories:
- Browser UX: "As a web product engineer, I want to render intermediate paragraphs as they arrive and show which chunks are 'finalized' vs 'tentative', with minimal reflow."
- Agent integration: "As a bot developer, I want to call an external knowledge search tool mid-stream and get a deterministic invocation id so I can reconcile side effects if reconnection happens."
- Mobile app: "As a mobile engineer, I want resumable sessions that avoid re-generating long transcripts and only request missing epochs on reconnect."

Design overview:
1) Epochal segmentation
   - Concept: The model server emits ordered epochs (monotonic epoch_id strings) that group tokens into semantically coherent blocks. Each epoch contains one or more SOMP frames and an optional text delta for free-form tokens.
   - Properties: epochs are ordered, durable (server retains last N epochs for resume), and commit markers indicate finality.
   - Example headers: {version:1,epoch_id:2025-10-03T12:03:45Z-0001,seq:3,final:false}

2) SOMP (Structured Output Micro-Protocol)
   - Lightweight frame structure (text-first JSON line-esque with constrained keys). Example frame types: "meta" (schema info), "action" (tool-call descriptor), "checkpoint" (minimal resume state), "error".
   - Field set (compact): v, eid, seq, type, payload_base64(optional), idempotency_token(optional), intent(optional).
   - Design rationale: text-friendly, easily logged, small; avoids nested heavy schema while allowing evolution via version field.

3) Tool-calling flow (non-blocking, epoch-aware)
   - Client SDK exposes async tool_call(action_descriptor). SDK attaches an idempotency_token and publishes a special SOMP action frame into the outgoing request context.
   - Server routes the action to configured tool adapter and emits two SOMP frames: "action-ack" (tool-call queued, includes call_id) and later "action-result" with the result or a retriable error. Action-result is attached to the epoch where it completes.
   - On reconnection, clients can query a per-session list of action states by call_id. The server guarantees stable call_ids for retained epochs.

4) Resumability and checkpoints
   - Checkpoint frames contain minimal KV-prefix snapshots (token offsets + small state blobs) encoded as base64. Checkpoints are optional and emitted only every M epochs or on explicit commit.
   - Rejoin flow: client supplies last_seen_epoch_id and optional last_tool_call_id; server responds with next epochs and any pending action-results.

5) SDK ergonomics
   - Primary surfaces: ProgressIterator (async), on_epoch(callback), tool_call(action) -> Promise<Result>, reconnect(retry_options) -> ProgressIterator.
   - Example usage (pseudo):
     const it = client.stream(prompt)
     for await (const epoch of it) {
       render(epoch.textDelta)
       if (epoch.somp?.actions) {
         epoch.somp.actions.forEach(a => attachUiAction(a))
       }
     }
   - Helpful defaults: automatic small window buffering (200ms), backoff policy for network jitter, and auto-attach idempotency tokens to tool calls.

6) Backpressure and QoS
   - On overload, server may emit a "throttle" SOMP frame for a session with suggested client_pause_ms. SDK honors it and surfaces a soft UI indicator.
   - Batching heuristics: server may coalesce small epochs for throughput; clients can request stricter latency (latency_budget header) to opt into smaller batches at higher cost.

7) Observability and logging
   - Epoch telemetry: epoch_emit_latency, epoch_commit_delay, epoch_size_bytes.
   - Tool-call telemetry: call_latency, call_retries, call_idempotency_violations.
   - Console: per-route epoch retention, percent of resumed sessions, failed-action-rate, and distribution of epoch sizes.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (internal alpha): SDK experiment for Node + Browser, server feature flag, retention N=50 epochs, no checkpointing by default.
- Phase 1 (private beta): expose SOMP frames in hosted-api v2 streaming endpoint, CLI tooling to inspect epochs, telemetry dashboard.
- Phase 2 (general availability): defaults enabled, checkpointing optional config, mobile client guides.

Metrics to validate:
- Client perceived time-to-first-finalized-epoch (target: <350ms median for typical prompts).
- Resume success rate (target: >99.5% after network blips).
- Tool-call duplication rate (target: <0.1% for idempotent adapters).
- Average epoch payload size (target: median <400 bytes).

Security & compliance considerations:
- Checkpoints may include minimal state; by default they exclude PII and sensitive keys. We will provide flags to redact and integrate with KMS policies for Private deployments.
- Action frames include idempotency tokens but not raw credentials; tool adapters are responsible for secret handling.

Open questions / risks:
- Retention sizing: how many epochs to retain for typical customer budgets? Storage cost vs resume usefulness needs experiments.
- SOMP versioning: what upgrade story for older clients when we change frame semantics? Provide clear backward-compatible additions and strict parsing rules.
- Tool side-effects: for non-idempotent tool adapters we need explicit compensation patterns; should the server provide a saga/compensation primitive?
- Mobile network behavior: frequency of checkpoints vs battery/network cost tradeoffs.

Next steps (concrete):
- Engineering spike: implement a lightweight epoch emitter in dev stack (2 weeks), measure epoch sizes on internal prompts.
- SDK prototype: async iterator + tool_call shim for Node/browser (2 weeks).
- UX sync: create a simple demo that renders tentative vs finalized epochs and triggers a search tool call mid-stream (1 week).
- Define retention defaults and storage cost estimates for Dedicated/Private customers (ops + pricing).

Appendix - example epoch sequence (simplified):
- epoch 0001: SOMP(meta v1), text: "Draft intro...", final:false
- epoch 0002: SOMP(action call id=ac-42 intent=search idempotency=tok-abc), text: "Running search..."
- epoch 0003: SOMP(action-ack call_id=ac-42 queued=true)
- epoch 0006: SOMP(action-result call_id=ac-42 status=ok payload_base64=eyJ0b3AiOiJIZXJlIn0=) , text: "Search found X results..."
- epoch 0010: SOMP(checkpoint kv=base64(...)), final:true

Notes to reviewers: look for portability across our current streaming SDKs and think about whether SOMP should be a separate content-type (application/somp+json) or carried as compact JSON lines in the stream.
